properties.name: Flame extinction
properties.description: Termination of combustion under specified chemical and transport conditions.

properties.name: Microgravity combustion
properties.description: Combustion studied under reduced buoyancy in a microgravity environment.

properties.name: Thermal radiation
properties.description: Radiant transfer of energy from flame, soot or heated surfaces.

properties.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments / Flame Design
properties.summary: ACME Flame Design investigates normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames, including soot inception, extinction and temperature structure. The final report identifies ethylene as the flight fuel except for one propane calibration day; proposed methane tests were not conducted. Separate normal- and inverse-flame tables preserve test identifiers and conditions. Adiabatic flame temperature is a calculated condition, not a measured peak flame temperature.

properties.title: ACME/Flame Design — investigation-level study
properties.summary: ACME Flame Design investigates normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames, including soot inception, extinction and temperature structure. The final report identifies ethylene as the flight fuel except for one propane calibration day; proposed methane tests were not conducted. Separate normal- and inverse-flame tables preserve test identifiers and conditions. Adiabatic flame temperature is a calculated condition, not a measured peak flame temperature.

conditions.hardware: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME), Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), Reconfiguration of Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
conditions.scope: Study-level description; not a single physical test.
conditions.observations_vs_objectives: Metadata objectives and hypotheses are not treated as measured findings.

methods: Spherical burner experiments on the ISS and in drop towers
Cameras, radiometers, photomultiplier tubes and thermocouples

properties.name: Spherical diffusion flames
properties.description: Non-premixed flames arranged approximately spherically around a source or sink.

properties.name: Soot formation
properties.description: Production and evolution of carbonaceous particles during combustion.

properties.title: PSI-10_Reports_FinalRpt_ACMEFlameDesign.pdf
properties.summary: The final report describes atmospheric-pressure ethylene experiments and transient simulations. It reports an extinction temperature near 1130 K and critical mass fluxes of 0.2 g/m²/s for normal flames and 0.68 g/m²/s for inverse flames. The reported values apply to that tested system. Flames with steady-state behavior were observed for up to 870 s; the much longer 100,000 s result is numerical. The flight program used ethylene except for one propane calibration day; proposed methane and CO2-diluent tests were not performed.

evidence.locator: metadata.objective
evidence.text: The primary objectives of this flight experiment are: A. Obtain soot-inception limits of quasi-steady normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames as functions of flow rate, Zst, amount of inert (N2 or CO2), and pressure for C2H4 and CH4 flames. Identify the corresponding temperatures in hot regions. Obtain similar limits and temperatures for inverse and normal coflow flames. B. Obtain detailed measurements in quasi-steady normal and inverse spherical diffusion flames for C2H4 and CH4. Determine the effects of flow rate, Zst, amount of N2, and pressure on flame temperature, size, color, and soot volume fraction. Evaluate the possible existence of steady flames. C. Obtain extinction limits as functions of Zst, amount of N2, and pressure for normal and inverse spherical C2H4 and CH4 flames. Identify the corresponding temperatures in hot regions. Identify the presence of radiative or kinetic extinction. Evaluate whether pseudo-flammability limits can be obtained for these flames.

evidence.locator: metadata.approach
evidence.text: Perform spherical diffusion flame tests in drop towers and aboard the International Space Station. Consider a broad range of reactant dilutions, flow rates and pressures for normal and inverse convection directions. Observe the flames with a broad suite of cameras, radiometers, photomultiplier tubes, and thermocouples.
